# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |

(empty)

I am establishing a fixed three-symbol code for Deaf: the first gesture means red, the second blue, and the third green. Deaf can then identify the engraved mark and tell Blind which color wire to cut.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "👌"])
```

| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a distinctive engraved symbol on the plate; its character has no spoken name, so I cannot read it aloud. Wires 1, 2, and 3 feel indistinguishable. I cannot feel useful display or light information. Do not yet tell me to cut.
Deaf says to Mute: Visual state: display 0; light off; plate engraved question mark; wires in order 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. Please match this to the manual and tell Blind the exact safe procedure.

The engraved mark reported by Deaf is a question mark, which is not any of the three marks listed in the manual. Therefore no wire color is authorized, and Blind must not cut. I will signal Deaf to stop and relay that no cut is safe or specified.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

| ꖜ | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 0, light off, plate engraved question mark; wires in order 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. Please identify the exact safe procedure from the manual, including which wire position to cut, if any.
Deaf says to Mute: I cannot assign a safe meaning to ✋ without an agreed code. Please speak the manual's exact procedure to Blind, using the visual state: display 0, light off, plate ?, wires red-blue-green.

The question mark is not one of the manual’s three marks, so the manual provides no authorized wire position. The exact safe procedure is to cut nothing. Deaf needs a clear stop signal; I am using the conventional stop gesture to mean “do not cut,” and he should state that procedure aloud to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

|---|---|

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still need the manual's exact safe procedure and the specific wire position, if a cut is required. I will not act on the plate question mark or cut while the procedure is unknown.
Deaf says to Mute: Please stop using the unagreed ✋ code. Speak the manual's exact instructions to Blind now, including which part to operate and the required result.

I cannot speak to Blind, and Deaf has rejected the previously attempted gesture code. The manual has no instruction for a question-mark engraving, so no wire position is authorized. Since any unagreed gesture could mislead Deaf, I will send nothing and preserve the safe state.

```text
wait()
```

Deaf says to Mute: Visible state unchanged: display 0, light off, plate ?, wires red-blue-green. Please confirm by speaking the exact manual procedure to Blind.

The manual lists only three engraved marks, and the observed question mark matches none of them. Thus no wire may safely be selected: the required action is no action. Because I cannot speak, I must convey this to Deaf visually; I will use a clear negative followed by the previously used stop symbol, with no wire-position gesture.

Deaf says to Mute: I can see your gestures, but 👎 ✋ have no agreed meaning. Please speak the manual's exact procedure to Blind, including the required action and confirmation.

The question mark is not among the manual’s three valid marks, so no cut is authorized. I cannot speak, and Deaf has not accepted any gesture code, so I cannot reliably transmit the instruction without risking a misinterpretation. I will not send an ambiguous signal.

Deaf says to Mute: Please use your speaking turn to give Blind the manual's exact procedure. The visible state is still display 0, light off, plate ?, wires red-blue-green.
